title: Count Orders by Status
description:
The orders table tracks the fulfillment status of every order. Count how many orders exist for each status.

**Table: orders** — `id`, `customer_id`, `status`, `order_date`

Return `status` and `order_count`. Order by `status`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE orders (id INT, customer_id INT, status VARCHAR, order_date DATE); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1,1,'pending','2026-01-05'),(2,2,'shipped','2026-01-10'),(3,3,'delivered','2026-01-15'),(4,4,'pending','2026-02-01'),(5,5,'shipped','2026-02-10'),(6,1,'delivered','2026-02-20'),(7,2,'cancelled','2026-03-01'),(8,3,'delivered','2026-03-10'),(9,4,'shipped','2026-03-15'),(10,5,'delivered','2026-03-20');
solution_sql: SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders GROUP BY status ORDER BY status

test_cases.description: 4 distinct statuses returned (cancelled, delivered, pending, shipped)

hints: Use GROUP BY status to collapse rows with the same status into one.
COUNT(*) counts all rows in each group.
explanation: GROUP BY status groups all rows that share the same status value. COUNT(*) then counts how many rows fall into each group, giving: cancelled=1, delivered=4, pending=2, shipped=3.
